skill.name: database-schema-designer
skill.description: Design and review SQL or NoSQL schemas using normalization, relationship, indexing, migration, integrity, and performance guidance.
skill.summary: Create maintainable data models, indexes, and migration plans for relational and document databases.

content.value_statement: Poor schemas cause inconsistent data, slow queries, and risky migrations. This skill guides SQL and NoSQL modeling, indexing, constraints, and migration planning.
actual_capabilities: Explains first, second, and third normal forms with relational examples.
Recommends data types, keys, constraints, and relationship patterns.
Compares document embedding and referencing for MongoDB models.
Develops indexing strategies for common query and sorting patterns.
Outlines reversible, backward-compatible, and zero-downtime migrations.
Provides a structured checklist for schema reviews and deployment readiness.
limitations: Provides guidance and templates but does not connect to or inspect a live database.
Does not benchmark queries, validate vendor syntax, or execute migrations.
Generic examples require adaptation to the selected database engine and application requirements.
Capacity estimates still require production data, workload measurements, and operational constraints.

use_cases.title: Model a new application
use_cases.description: Define entities, relationships, constraints, and indexes for a new transactional service.

use_cases.title: Review an existing schema
use_cases.description: Identify normalization, integrity, and query performance issues before a major release.

use_cases.title: Plan a production migration
use_cases.description: Structure compatible rollout, backfill, validation, and rollback stages for schema changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic relational model
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a relational schema for {application}. Include entities, primary keys, foreign keys, cardinalities, and essential constraints. Explain each design choice.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a new application with clear business entities.

prompt_templates.title: Review schema quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this schema for normalization, integrity, and maintainability: {schema}. List issues by priority and propose concrete changes for {database_engine}.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve an existing schema before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Design an indexing strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these queries and workload details, design an indexing strategy: {queries_and_workload}. Explain column order, write costs, and indexes to avoid.
prompt_templates.scenario: Optimize known access patterns without excessive indexing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a zero-downtime migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a zero-downtime migration from {current_schema} to {target_schema} on {database_engine}. Include rollout stages, backfill, validation, rollback, and compatibility risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Change a production schema while older application versions remain active.

output_examples.input: Design an order management schema for customers, products, orders, and line items.
output: The proposal separates customers, orders, products, and order items.
Each relationship includes cardinality, referential actions, and integrity constraints.
An index plan covers customer history, order status, and product lookup queries.
A migration sequence introduces tables and constraints in reversible stages.

output_examples.input: Choose embedding or referencing for customer orders in a document database.
output: The recommendation references customers because their profiles change independently.
Small order items remain embedded because they are read with each order.
Document growth limits and update patterns define when items should move to a separate collection.

output_examples.input: Review a migration that immediately renames a required production column.
output: The review identifies compatibility and locking risks.
A staged approach adds the new column, dual-writes data, backfills rows, validates results, and removes the old column later.
The rollback plan preserves both columns until all application versions use the replacement.

best_practices: Provide access patterns, write volume, data growth, and database engine before requesting a design.
Validate generated constraints and migrations against staging data before production use.
Measure query plans and index costs with representative workloads after implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not copy generic SQL without checking database-specific syntax and locking behavior.
Do not add indexes without documenting supported queries and write costs.
Do not perform destructive migrations without backups, validation steps, and a tested rollback plan.

faq.question: Does this skill support SQL and NoSQL databases?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers relational normalization and constraints, plus document embedding, referencing, indexing, and scaling considerations.

faq.question: Does it create production-ready schemas?
faq.answer: It creates design guidance and examples. Engineers must validate syntax, capacity, security, and operational behavior for their database engine.

faq.question: Can it review an existing schema?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the schema, database engine, important queries, data volume, and known problems for a focused review.

faq.question: Does it execute migrations?
faq.answer: No. It outlines migration stages and templates but does not connect to databases or run commands.

faq.question: Can it recommend indexes?
faq.answer: Yes. Include representative queries and workload details so recommendations reflect filters, sorting, selectivity, and write costs.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Describe classifications and access needs without sharing real secrets. Apply encryption, least privilege, parameterized queries, and database-specific controls.
